output.summary: Deterministic verdict preserved: run_validity VALID, policy_verdict PASS, analysis_coverage COMPLETE, and capacity_summary reports bound_type BOUNDED on load_axis users (unit count) with lower_inclusive 197 and upper_exclusive 297, policy_verdict PASS. Step-1 (target 100) PASS at p05_10s 97, step-2 (target 200) PASS at p05_10s 197, step-3 (target 300) FAIL at p05_10s 297 because response_time_p95_ms observed 420 exceeded threshold 250; the stage-3 window business_verdict is FAIL while the run-level verdict remains PASS. All three generator-cpu diagnostic guards (effect diagnostic, threshold 0.85) PASSed with generator cpu_used around 0.41-0.45 ratio, so the generator was not flagged saturated. resource_verdict is NO_POLICY in all three windows. capacity_knee is null with knee_reason KNEE_DETECTOR_NOT_IMPLEMENTED (a fixed product limitation). clock_alignment is not_verified_by_core; the evaluation window and run window share start epoch 1767225600000 with a 500 ms trailing difference (run_to_epoch_ms 1767226500500 vs evaluation_to_epoch_ms 1767226500000). Overall metric summary reports error_count 0 and sample_count 3601 with latency_ms p95 417 and max 1500.

hypotheses.observation: capacity_summary reports bound_type BOUNDED with lower_inclusive 197 and upper_exclusive 297 (load_axis users, unit count); step-2 verified_bound_load is 197 with verdict PASS and step-3 verified_bound_load is 297 with verdict FAIL.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: The load range that satisfies the latency policy is bounded between roughly 197 and 297 users, but the exact maximum is not identified by the supplied graded steps.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Run additional graded load steps between 197 and 297 users (for example 220, 250, 275) and let the policy checks re-evaluate at each step to narrow the boundary; keep the existing deterministic verdict unchanged.

hypotheses.observation: The response_time_p95_ms policy checks observed 140 ms (threshold 250) in both stage-1 and stage-2, and 420 ms in stage-3, whose window business_verdict is FAIL.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: Latency increased nonlinearly between the ~200-user and ~300-user steps, consistent with saturation or queueing near the capacity boundary; this is a hypothesis and not a proven cause.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Inspect per-interval latency percentiles and any system-under-test resource telemetry across the 197-297 user range, and add intermediate load steps to find where p95 begins approaching 250 ms.

hypotheses.observation: The generator-cpu diagnostic guard (effect diagnostic, operator gt, threshold 0.85) PASSed in all three stages while generator cpu_used stayed around 0.41-0.45 ratio across the stage-1, stage-2, and stage-3 windows.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: The load generator was not near its diagnostic CPU threshold, so the observed latency limit is not attributable to generator CPU saturation; no system-under-test resource series is referenced to explain the stage-3 latency rise.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Collect or inspect system-under-test CPU, memory, and network telemetry for the stage-3 window to test whether a resource exhaustion coincides with the p95 exceedance.

hypotheses.observation: resource_binding reports clock_alignment not_verified_by_core with evaluation_from_epoch_ms 1767225600000, evaluation_to_epoch_ms 1767226500000, run_to_epoch_ms 1767226500500, and dropped_leading/trailing cells 0.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: Until clock alignment is verified, stage-to-stage or resource-to-latency ordering cannot support a temporal causal interpretation across the generator and any monitored components.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Verify clock synchronization between the load generator, sampler hosts, and any monitored system before drawing ordering or lead/lag conclusions from the windowed series.

hypotheses.observation: metric-summary-overall reports error_count 0 and sample_count 3601 with latency_ms p95 417 and max 1500, while the stage-3 policy check observed response_time_p95_ms 420 against threshold 250.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: The absence of recorded errors does not by itself explain the p95 exceedance; high latency can occur without client-visible errors, but the referenced data do not prove either cause.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Inspect per-interval and per-sampler latency distributions to identify when the max 1500 ms and p95 420 ms values occurred and which windows contributed to them.

recommendations.action: Rerun or extend the load test with intermediate graded steps between 197 and 297 users to locate the capacity boundary more precisely.
recommendations.rationale: capacity_summary provides lower_inclusive 197 (step-2 PASS at verified_bound_load 197) and upper_exclusive 297 (step-3 FAIL at verified_bound_load 297); the step granularity does not identify the exact maximum load that passes the latency policy.

recommendations.action: Verify clock alignment across the load generator, sampler hosts, and any monitored systems before interpreting ordering or temporal relationships.
recommendations.rationale: resource_binding reports clock_alignment not_verified_by_core; an unverified clock relationship cannot support lead/lag or temporal causal hypotheses.

recommendations.action: Inspect or collect system-under-test resource telemetry for the stage-3 window; the referenced analysis contains only generator active_users and cpu_used series.
recommendations.rationale: The generator-cpu diagnostic guard PASSed in all stages with cpu_used near 0.43 ratio against a 0.85 threshold, so the generator was not flagged saturated; capacity analysis should therefore focus on the system under test, whose resource series are absent from this analysis.

recommendations.action: If resource-based SLA verdicts are desired for these windows, configure an applicable resource rule with effect sla; note that NO_POLICY remains NO_POLICY until a rule is evaluated.
recommendations.rationale: Each window_policy_summary reports resource_verdict NO_POLICY; missing policy is distinct from PASS and FAIL, and no resource SLA rule was in effect for these windows.

recommendations.action: Take no corrective action on capacity_knee; it is null with knee_reason KNEE_DETECTOR_NOT_IMPLEMENTED, which is a fixed product limitation.
recommendations.rationale: The capacity bound is derived from stages with verified product outcomes independently of any knee; implementing or enabling a knee detector is not a product-provided or user-performed step.

caveats: capacity_knee is null with knee_reason KNEE_DETECTOR_NOT_IMPLEMENTED; this is a fixed product limitation and neither a defect of the run nor a step the operator can take.
The generator CPU rule has effect diagnostic; its PASS in all stages is diagnostic by contract and does not create an upper capacity bound nor prove the system under test is healthy.
resource_verdict NO_POLICY in all windows means no applicable resource SLA rule was evaluated; NO_POLICY, PASS, and FAIL are distinct, and NO_POLICY is not a pass.
clock_alignment is not_verified_by_core; the epoch windows overlap the run (shared start 1767225600000, trailing run delta 500 ms to 1767226500500), but no synchronized clock relationship is proven.
Run-level figures (sample_count 3601, error_count 0) and per-window policy metrics measure different scopes; they are not directly comparable and do not establish absence of a problem.
Only load-generator telemetry is referenced; no system-under-test resource series is present, so all capacity and latency explanations remain hypotheses.
analysis_coverage is COMPLETE, but that refers to the evaluation of the supplied policies and does not expand the referenced evidence types (no SUT telemetry, no clock verification).
The deterministic verdict (PASS with BOUNDED capacity 197 inclusive to 297 exclusive) is preserved; this advice never changes the verdict.
The overall latency metrics (p95 417, max 1500) aggregate the whole run including the failing stage and are not window-level observations.
